_doc: Short hand-written explanation of each FAIL row for docs/equiv_failures.md (verdicts.py). The full trace stays in the row's .nonmatching.txt note. Remove an entry when its row stops failing.
0040b0f0: Every mismatching input has a face with more than 4 vertices, or 0
A face holds at most 4 (shape.h w[4]), so both builds index past a 4-entry local array into stack they lay out differently
Inputs with 1 to 4 vertices all match (3864 valid on a 6000-input run, 58/58 edges)
Such faces cannot exist in the game: face::load 0x408d60 would overwrite the count itself
Verdict: harness artefact, not a source bug
0047ff60: rgl::mesh::add_vertex 0x413c50 (original code in both builds) copies a vertex from a stack temporary it never fully initialises
Vertex dwords +0x24/+0x2c are whatever earlier calls left on the stack: a return address, different in each binary
compute_tangents 0x41ce80 does arithmetic on them, so one build gets NaN and the other a finite value
Verdict: the original's value is indeterminate, not a source bug
004e05c0: The recorded run is from before the uninitialised-in-both rule (5c30f72)
Traced 2026-11-01: both builds make the same 326 calls with the same arguments
Every differing word is a vector4 w lane nothing ever writes, or a stale stack matrix word, copied on by original code (text_rect 0x49b4f0, add_quad 0x44f5f0)
Under the new rule there is no mismatch, but the function is too slow to finish enough inputs for a verdict
004eb3c0: The first virtual call (0x4eb3f6) goes through a random vtable slot that lands in the middle of original code
That code passes the call's return address to the SendMessageA model, which differs between the two binaries (0.05 vs 0 stored)
A real slider vtable slot is always a method, so this cannot happen in the game
Only 13% of instructions are covered; the rest was checked by reading the disassembly
004f1460: The only memory difference is the w lane of two 4-float temporaries copied to +0x168/+0x190
The original loads that w from a stack slot nothing writes (0x4f24f6/0x4f252f)
The recorded run is from before the uninitialised-in-both rule, and the function is too slow to finish enough inputs for a new verdict
004faee0: ShadowMap::read_pixel 0x4641a0 (original code in both builds) reads the pointer that D3D LockRect should have written
The harness does not model LockRect, so each build dereferences its own stack leftover and the depth compare diverges
A real LockRect always writes the pointer
0052f250: The original reads a stack slot it never writes (the harness fills it with 0xcccccccc, shown as -107374176.0)
Our compiler puts that temporary in the same slot as a local it has just zeroed, so ours reads 0
Fixing it would need stack-slot tricks, which we don't do
Verdict: the original's value is indeterminate
